title: Real-Time In-Situ TEM Insights into the Electrochemical Behavior of Hybrid Polymer Network Cathodes in Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
content: Lithium-sulfur (Li–S) batteries are considered one of the most promising candidates for next-generation energy storage devices due to their theoretical high energy density, low cost, and abundance of sulfur. Despite these advantages, the practical application of Li–S batteries has been hindered by several challenges, the most significant being the dissolution of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) into the electrolyte, which results in poor cycle stability and low efficiency [1]. To mitigate these issues, the development of advanced cathode materials that can confine sulfur and reduce polysulfide dissolution is critical. Hybrid polymer network cathodes have shown great promise in addressing these challenges by providing a stable matrix for sulfur incorporation and minimizing polysulfide migration [2, 3].
